subject: Clarify: Do you train on customer data? Retention & deletion process
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on model training and retention windows

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups before we proceed to procurement: specifically, does Redwood ever use customer prompt/response content to train or improve models? If not, can you confirm this in writing and explain the retention windows for request logs, cache/KV data, and backups?

Also attached is our standard security questionnaire — most of it is small stuff but the training/use section is important to our legal team. Please review and point me to any clauses we should expect in the contract.

Thanks,

Head of Platform Security
Acme Robotics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on model training and retention windows

Hi Jane — thanks for sending this over and for the good questions. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer prompts, completions, or other customer content to train or improve our public/private models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement. I'll expand below with the practical retention/deletion timelines and contract options.

1) Training usage assurance
- No training without opt-in: We will not ingest customer content into any model training datasets (offline or online) unless there is an explicit contractual opt-in. This applies to Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Telemetry and aggregated metrics: We collect aggregate telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) for product and reliability improvements. That telemetry is not linkable to raw prompt/response text.

2) Retention windows (default enterprise settings)
- Request/response bodies (raw): Default retention: 30 days. This is used for billing dispute resolution and abuse detection.
- Short-term caches / KV: Evicted within 24 hours in normal operation; cache entries are per-request and not retained long-term.
- System logs & traces: 90 days by default (can be adjusted by enterprise plan).
- Backups / snapshots: Backups are retained for up to 90 days; customer data scheduled for deletion will be excluded from new backups immediately, but historical backup copies are rotated/purged on the typical backup retention window.

3) Deletion process
- Deletion API: We provide a deletion endpoint and a DPA clause that instructs us to purge customer data on request. Typical flow: primary storage purge within 24 hours; cache and index purge within 24 hours; backups marked for deletion and purged according to backup retention (up to 90 days) unless a shorter contractual requirement is agreed.
- Audit trail: We generate an audit record when we process a deletion request. That audit record contains metadata about the action (who, when, request id) but does not retain the deleted content.

4) Contract options
- We can add explicit 'no-training' language to the DPA and Services Agreement.
- For Dedicated/Private customers we offer options to disable request logging entirely (subject to limited diagnostic windows) and to pin retention windows in contract.

I'll attach our DPA and a short sample of the deletion API call. Let me know which pieces you'd like formalized in the contract and we can route to Legal/Compliance.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on model training and retention windows

Hi Jane — Monica from Legal/Privacy here. A few clarifying items from a contractual perspective:

- We are comfortable including a clear "no-use-for-training" covenant in the Services Agreement and DPA. The clause will state that Redwood will not use customer content to train models or improve model parameters unless Customer provides a written opt-in.
- We can also include retention SLAs: e.g., "primary data purged from active storage within 24 hours, caches cleared within 24 hours, backups purged within X days" — we are able to contractually set X to 30/60/90 depending on your needs.
- For regulators/customers that require zero-logging, we offer a Dedicated/Private deployment with disabled request logging and the option to hold logs only in your VPC.

If Acme has specific language in your questionnaire you want us to mirror, paste the exact text and we'll propose redlines. Otherwise, we'll propose the standard DPA redline that aligns with the above.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Jane — quick technical addendum on the deletion mechanics so your engineers have the detail: 

- Deletion API sample: POST /v1/customers/{customer_id}/data/delete with a request id. When invoked we run a three-stage purge: 1) mark records for immediate removal from primary stores and queues (committed within minutes), 2) invalidate caches and KV within 24 hours, 3) schedule backup sweep where snapshots containing the data are rotated out based on the backup retention window (default 90 days; can be reduced contractually).
- Indexes & derived artifacts: We do not materialize customer data into shared model weights. If a customer elects to allow data to be used for model improvement we will only do so under explicit data pipeline controls; otherwise, no derivations from customer prompts are added to training corpora.
- Verification: After a deletion we can run a verification job and provide a signed attestation that the purge workflow completed for a given request id. The attestation includes timestamps and the storage identifiers removed (not the content).

If you want, I can share a short script that calls the deletion endpoint and polls for completion — attached.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Redwood Inference
